# Proverbs 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** My child, don't forget what I've taught you — hold onto my instructions with everything you've got,

**2** Because they will add years to your life and bring you genuine peace.

**3** Never let loyalty and honesty slip away from you. Wear them like a necklace; engrave them deep in your heart.

**4** Then you'll earn a reputation that both God and people respect.

**5** Trust the LORD completely — don't rely on what you think you know.

**6** Include Him in everything you do, and He will guide you down the right road.

**7** Don't assume you've got it all figured out. Respect the LORD and walk away from what's wrong.

**8** That will bring health to your body and strength to your bones.

**9** Give the LORD the best of what you have — the first portion of everything you earn,

**10** And you'll find your storerooms overflowing and your wine vats spilling over.

**11** My child, don't resent it when the LORD corrects you, and don't get discouraged by His discipline,

**12** Because the LORD only corrects people He loves — the way a good father disciplines a beloved child.

**13** How fortunate is the person who finds wisdom — the one who gains genuine understanding!

**14** Because what she offers is worth more than a silver mine, and her returns outperform gold.

**15** She's more valuable than rubies — nothing you could ever want compares to her.

**16** In one hand she holds long life; in the other, wealth and honor.

**17** Every road she takes you down is enjoyable, and every path she walks leads to peace.

**18** She is a tree of life for anyone who embraces her — hold onto her, and you will be truly happy.

**19** The LORD used wisdom when He built the earth; He set the sky in place with understanding.

**20** By what He knows, the underground waters broke through, and the clouds release their rain.

**21** My child, keep these truths in front of you always — hold onto good judgment and careful thinking,

**22** And they will breathe life into you and be an ornament that makes you shine.

**23** Then you'll walk through life confidently, without tripping over obstacles.

**24** When you go to bed, you won't lie there anxious; your sleep will be deep and restful.

**25** You won't panic when something sudden happens, or when disaster strikes the wicked,

**26** Because the LORD Himself will be your security, and He'll make sure you don't get trapped.

**27** Don't hold back something good from someone who needs it, when you're perfectly able to help.

**28** Don't tell your neighbor, 'Come back tomorrow and I'll help you then' — when you could help right now.

**29** Don't plot to harm your neighbor, when that person lives beside you in good faith.

**30** Don't pick a fight with someone who hasn't done anything to you.

**31** Don't look at violent people and wish you were like them. Don't follow any of their ways,

**32** Because the LORD detests people who are crooked, but He shares His friendship with those who are honest.

**33** The LORD's curse falls on the house of the wicked, but He pours blessings on where the righteous live.

**34** He mocks those who mock, but shows kindness to those who are humble.

**35** Wise people will be honored, but fools will carry nothing but shame.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:5-6**: This is one of the most beloved passages in the entire Bible — and it's more radical than it sounds. It's not about ignoring reason; it's about refusing to make your own cleverness the final authority.

- **3:12**: The comparison to a father's discipline is meant to be comforting, not threatening. It means God cares enough to correct.

- **3:19-20**: A quick, stunning pivot — suddenly the text connects personal wisdom to cosmic creation. The same wisdom that guides your life built the universe.

— PNEUMA
